obligations.statement: For an embedded n-dimensional submanifold of codimension k at least one, the ambient Bochner Laplacian of an extension of a tangent vector field satisfies the arbitrary-codimension Gauss formulas (1.5) and (1.6) at the chosen point.

For an embedded n-dimensional submanifold of codimension k at least one, the ambient and intrinsic Hodge Laplacians of an extension of a tangent vector field satisfy the arbitrary-codimension Gauss formula of Corollary 1.20.
obligations.locator: arXiv:2212.11928v2, Corollary 1.20 and equation (1.26) for the hypersurface specialization

obligations.statement: On every complete noncompact bounded-geometry surface with Gaussian curvature K at most -kappa squared, deformation-viscosity Navier-Stokes with mu positive and initial datum u0 in H admits a global weak solution in L-infinity(0,T;H) intersect L2(0,T;V) for every T positive.
obligations.locator: arXiv:2605.17502v2, Theorem 6.1, first conclusion after equation (39)

obligations.statement: The global weak solution supplied by Theorem 6.1 is unique in the stated L-infinity(0,T;H) intersect L2(0,T;V) solution class.
obligations.locator: arXiv:2605.17502v2, Theorem 6.1 and its uniqueness argument

obligations.statement: The weak solution supplied by Theorem 6.1 admits a pressure distribution in D'((0,T) times M) that recovers the momentum equation.
The weak solution supplied by Theorem 6.1 satisfies squared L2 energy decay bounded by exp(-2 mu kappa squared t) times the squared L2 norm of u0.
obligations.locator: arXiv:2605.17502v2, Theorem 6.1, equation (40), derived in equations (41)-(45)

obligations.statement: For every smooth tangential solenoidal field on the canonical torus and either endpoint wall law, there exists a smooth shell recovery that is exactly solenoidal, has zero normal trace on both walls, and satisfies the corresponding natural wall trace.
obligations.locator: Project specialization of arXiv:2605.20589v3, Theorem 4.5 (M2), Proposition 3.2, Section 3.4, and Appendix A.4

obligations.statement: The canonical-torus smooth shell recovery has exact normalized transverse-flux identification P_epsilon U_epsilon = v.
obligations.locator: Project specialization of arXiv:2605.20589v3, Theorem 4.5 (M2), with the repository's normalized flux map

obligations.statement: For every smooth tangential solenoidal field on the canonical torus and either endpoint, the squared shell L2 distance from the constant tangential lift is bounded by C epsilon squared times the squared C1 norm of the field.
obligations.locator: Project smooth-core estimate corresponding to arXiv:2605.20589v3, Theorem 4.5 (M2), after the half-thickness rescaling documented in docs/thin-shell-convergence.md

obligations.statement: For every smooth tangential solenoidal field on the canonical torus and either endpoint, the absolute shell-to-surface energy error is bounded by C epsilon squared times the squared C2 norm of the field.
obligations.locator: Project specialization of the smooth-data rate in arXiv:2605.20589v3, Theorem 4.5 (M2), with the canonical-torus coefficient bounds documented in docs/thin-shell-convergence.md

obligations.statement: For each of the deformation and Hodge form pairs on the source's torus-type surfaces of revolution, weak varying-space convergence U_epsilon to u implies liminf Q_epsilon(U_epsilon) at least Q0(u).
For each of the deformation and Hodge form pairs and every solenoidal surface form-domain field v, there is a solenoidal shell recovery converging strongly to v whose form energy converges to Q0(v).
For smooth surface fields, the recovery sequence in Theorem 4.5 has shell energy Q_epsilon equal to Q0 plus O(epsilon squared), for both endpoint form pairs.
The deformation and Hodge shell and surface forms on their solenoidal subspaces have associated nonnegative self-adjoint operators L_epsilon and L0.
For every lambda positive, the resolvents (L_epsilon + lambda)^(-1) converge strongly to (L0 + lambda)^(-1) for both endpoint form pairs.
The semigroups exp(-t L_epsilon) converge strongly to exp(-t L0), uniformly for t in compact time intervals, for both endpoint form pairs.
On each fixed azimuthal mode, bounded sequences are precompact and the eigenvalues of L_epsilon converge with multiplicity to the corresponding surface eigenvalues.
The shell forms satisfy the epsilon-uniform quadratic lower bound in the azimuthal mode number stated in Corollary 4.6.

Below every fixed spectral threshold only an epsilon-independent finite set of azimuthal modes contributes, so the full spectrum converges with multiplicity and no high-mode spectral pollution occurs.
obligations.locator: arXiv:2605.20589v3, Corollary 4.6, counting-function and no-pollution conclusion

obligations.statement: A smooth divergence-free stationary deformation-viscosity solution on HN(-a squared) with finite Dirichlet integral vanishes when N is three or four.
When N is two, the same stationary solution with the additional L-infinity assumption is an L2 harmonic gradient dF.
When N is at least five, the same stationary solution with the additional L-infinity assumption vanishes.
obligations.locator: arXiv:1501.04928v1, Theorem 1.1, N at least 5 conclusion

obligations.statement: For every R0 and a positive, the hyperbolic exterior domain admits a nontrivial steady Stokes solution with zero boundary trace, finite Dirichlet integral, distributional coclosedness, and pressure in L2_loc.
The steady Stokes solution constructed in Theorem 1.2 is not dF for any harmonic function F.

For every R0 and a positive, the hyperbolic exterior domain admits a nontrivial steady Navier-Stokes solution with zero boundary trace, finite Dirichlet integral, distributional coclosedness, and pressure in L2_loc.
The steady Navier-Stokes solution constructed in Theorem 1.3 is not dF for any harmonic function F.
